tldr: Bangkok's headlines collectively anchor on the all-50-districts disaster declaration as the defining fact, with the scale of displacement (52,000 homes, thousands in shelters) as the close second register. A narrower tier of headlines — concentrated in wire services and Asian regional press — surfaces a distinctly political dimension: a government-declared civil service holiday could delay a court ruling on disputed February election results.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to lead its headline with a death count ('At least two killed') rather than displacement scale or disaster-declaration framing.
Only outlet to place PM Anutin's interrupted diplomatic trip in the headline, introducing a governance-accountability angle absent from all other outlet headlines.
Only outlet to foreground early-warning failure in the headline ('came too late'), framing the event as a governance failure rather than a natural disaster.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, coverage converges on a single dominant register — disaster-declaration language ('flood disaster zone,' 'Katastrophenfall,' 'estado de desastre') appears across virtually every bucket — with the electoral court-delay angle visible only in wire and Asian regional headlines and invisible to most of the world's front pages.
